Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	"""Append-only local key vault.
2	
3	The vault persists an append-only version manifest (``manifest.json``) plus
4	one material file per sealed version under ``materials/``.  Revocations live
5	in their own append-only journal (``revocations.jsonl``): revoking a version
6	only appends a record, never deleting or altering historical material.
7	Repointing the active version (``set_active``) likewise appends one record
8	to its own journal (``activations.jsonl``), created on the first repoint and
9	simply absent from a vault that was never repointed.  ``reload()`` re-reads
10	and validates the whole keyring, both journals included, and swaps the
11	in-memory snapshot atomically; readers only ever see a complete old or
12	complete new snapshot.
13	
14	Besides direct sealing (``seal``), a version's material may be derived from
15	a passphrase with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (``derive_seal``).  The passphrase
16	itself is never persisted: only the derived bytes go through the ordinary
17	seal path, and the salt, iteration count and derived length travel with the
18	version's manifest record so the parameters can be queried (``derivation``)
19	and re-checked on reload.
20	
21	Multiple processes may share one vault directory.  Every operation that
22	reads from or writes to the disk state (open, seal, derive_seal, revoke,
23	set_active, reload) runs under an exclusive, blocking file lock held on
24	``vault.lock`` inside the vault directory (``fcntl.flock`` where available,
25	``msvcrt.locking`` on Windows — standard library only).  A writer waits
26	until it holds the lock and completes its whole record before releasing it,
27	so interleaved seals, revokes and repoints from different processes never
28	duplicate or skip a version number and never overwrite or truncate
29	historical material.  The lock file is only a mutual-exclusion device: it
30	carries no key data and plays no part in manifest or material validation.
31	``close()`` releases the lock file handle; the next operation reopens it and
32	reacquires the same lock, with no observable change in behaviour.

170	                journal_path = self._root / REVOCATIONS_NAME
171	                if not journal_path.exists():
172	                    # A vault created before revocations existed simply has
173	                    # an empty journal; the journal is append-only and never
174	                    # rewritten.
175	                    _atomic_write(journal_path, b"")
176	                self._snapshot, self._manifest = self._load_validated()
177	        except BaseException:
178	            self._release_lock_file()
179	            raise

186	        """Release the lock file handle.
187	
188	        Idempotent: closing an already-released vault is a no-op.  The next
189	        operation reopens ``vault.lock`` and reacquires the same exclusive
190	        lock, so observable behaviour is unchanged.
191	        """
192	        with self._lock:
193	            self._release_lock_file()

195	    def seal(self, key_id: str, material: bytes) -> int:
196	        """Store ``material`` as a new version of ``key_id``; return the version."""
197	        _check_key_id(key_id)
198	        if not isinstance(material, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
199	            raise TypeError("material must be a bytes-like object")

202	    def derive_seal(
203	        self,
204	        key_id: str,
205	        password: bytes,
206	        salt: bytes,
207	        iterations: int,
208	        length: int,
209	    ) -> int:
210	        """Derive material with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 and seal it as a version.
211	
212	        The passphrase is fed to the standard-library PBKDF2 implementation
213	        and never persisted: only the derived bytes go through the ordinary
214	        append-only seal path.  ``salt``, ``iterations`` and ``length`` are
215	        recorded alongside the version and can be queried with
216	        :meth:`derivation`.  Returns the new version number.
217	        """
218	        _check_key_id(key_id)
219	        password = _check_password(password)
220	        salt = _check_salt(salt)
221	        _check_derivation_int(iterations, "iterations")
222	        _check_derivation_int(length, "length")
223	        material = _derive_material(password, salt, iterations, length)
224	        parameters = {"salt": salt, "iterations": iterations, "length": length}

227	    def derivation(
228	        self, key_id: str, version: int | None = None
229	    ) -> dict:
230	        """Return a version's derivation parameters.
231	
232	        Returns ``{"salt": bytes, "iterations": int, "length": int}`` for a
233	        version produced by :meth:`derive_seal`, or an empty record ``{}``
234	        for a version sealed directly from supplied material.  With
235	        ``version=None`` the active version is queried.  Raises ``ValueError``
236	        for an empty key id, ``TypeError`` for a non-integer version, and
237	        ``KeyError`` for an unknown key or a version that does not exist —
238	        the same read semantics as the revocation queries.
239	        """
240	        _check_key_id(key_id)
241	        if version is not None:
242	            _check_version(version)
243	        entry = self._snapshot.get(key_id)
244	        if entry is None:
245	            raise KeyError(key_id)
246	        wanted = entry["active"] if version is None else version
247	        if wanted not in entry["versions"]:
248	            raise KeyError(f"{key_id!r} version {wanted!r}")
249	        parameters = entry["derivations"].get(wanted)
250	        return {} if parameters is None else dict(parameters)

252	    def load(self, key_id: str, version: int | None = None) -> bytes:
253	        """Return the stored material for ``key_id`` (active version by default).
254	
255	        With ``version=None`` the active version is read.  Entry validation
256	        matches the other per-version reads: the key id is checked first, so
257	        an empty key id raises ``ValueError`` before the version is looked at,
258	        and a non-integer version raises ``TypeError`` — bools and floats do
259	        not count, even a float numerically equal to an existing version.
260	        An unknown key or a genuine-int version that does not exist raises
261	        ``KeyError``.
262	        """
263	        _check_key_id(key_id)
264	        if version is not None:
265	            _check_version(version)
266	        snapshot = self._snapshot
267	        entry = snapshot.get(key_id)
268	        if entry is None:
269	            raise KeyError(key_id)
270	        wanted = entry["active"] if version is None else version
271	        try:
272	            return entry["versions"][wanted]
273	        except KeyError:
274	            raise KeyError(f"{key_id!r} version {wanted!r}") from None
275	
276	    def versions(self, key_id: str) -> list[int]:
277	        """Return the recorded versions of ``key_id``, ascending."""
278	        entry = self._snapshot.get(key_id)
279	        if entry is None:
280	            return []
281	        return sorted(entry["versions"])

283	    def active(self, key_id: str) -> int:
284	        """Return the active version of ``key_id``.
285	
286	        Normally the most recently sealed version; ``set_active`` can repoint
287	        it at an older historical version until the next seal.
288	        """
289	        entry = self._snapshot.get(key_id)
290	        if entry is None:
291	            raise KeyError(key_id)
292	        return entry["active"]

294	    def set_active(self, key_id: str, version: int) -> None:
295	        """Repoint the active version of ``key_id`` at historical ``version``.
296	
297	        Appends one record to the append-only ``activations.jsonl`` journal
298	        (created on the first repoint) without rewriting the manifest or any
299	        material.  The last record for a key wins while it still concerns the
300	        key's latest sealed version: sealing another version afterwards makes
301	        that new version active again, exactly as if the key had never been
302	        repointed.  Repointing at the version already active raises
303	        ``ValueError``, as does repointing at a revoked version; a version
304	        revoked *after* being pointed at is not an error.
305	        """
306	        _check_key_id(key_id)
307	        _check_version(version)
308	
309	        with self._locked():
310	            # Re-read and validate the persisted keyring under the
311	            # inter-process lock, exactly like revoke: the unknown/version/
312	            # revoked/active checks and the appended record must reflect the
313	            # latest journals on disk, including records other processes
314	            # appended.
315	            snapshot, disk_manifest = self._load_validated()
316	            entry = snapshot.get(key_id)
317	            if entry is None:
318	                raise KeyError(key_id)
319	            if version not in entry["versions"]:
320	                raise KeyError(f"{key_id!r} version {version!r}")
321	            if version in entry["revoked"]:
322	                raise ValueError(
323	                    f"{key_id!r} version {version!r} is revoked"
324	                )
325	            if version == entry["active"]:
326	                raise ValueError(
327	                    f"{key_id!r} version {version!r} is already the active "
328	                    "version"
329	                )
330	
331	            # ``latest`` binds this repoint to the key's current newest
332	            # sealed version.  On reload a repoint only applies while its
333	            # bound latest still matches the newest sealed version, so a
334	            # later seal silently supersedes it without touching this
335	            # append-only journal.
336	            latest = max(entry["versions"])
337	            record = {"key_id": key_id, "version": version, "latest": latest}
338	            line = (json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
339	            activations_path = self._root / ACTIVATIONS_NAME
340	            # Append-only; "ab" also creates the journal on the very first
341	            # repoint of a vault that simply had no such file before.
342	            with open(activations_path, "ab") as fh:
343	                fh.write(line)
344	                fh.flush()
345	                os.fsync(fh.fileno())
346	
347	            entry["active"] = version
348	            self._snapshot = snapshot
349	            self._manifest = disk_manifest
350	
351	    def revoke(self, key_id: str, version: int) -> None:
352	        """Mark ``version`` of ``key_id`` as revoked.
353	
354	        Revocation is an explicit marker only: the version's material stays
355	        readable, it stays in the version list, and the active version is
356	        unchanged.  The marker is appended to an append-only journal, so it
357	        survives a full ``reload()``.
358	        """
359	        _check_key_id(key_id)
360	        _check_version(version)
361	
362	        with self._locked():
363	            # Re-read and validate the persisted keyring under the
364	            # inter-process lock so the duplicate/unknown checks and the
365	            # appended record reflect the latest journal on disk, including
366	            # revocations appended by other processes.
367	            snapshot, disk_manifest = self._load_validated()
368	            entry = snapshot.get(key_id)
369	            if entry is None:
370	                raise KeyError(key_id)
371	            if version not in entry["versions"]:
372	                raise KeyError(f"{key_id!r} version {version!r}")
373	            if version in entry["revoked"]:
374	                raise ValueError(
375	                    f"{key_id!r} version {version!r} is already revoked"
376	                )
377	
378	            record = {"key_id": key_id, "version": version}
379	            line = (json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
380	            journal_path = self._root / REVOCATIONS_NAME
381	            if not journal_path.exists():
382	                # The journal is created when the vault opens; its absence
383	                # means it was removed out of band.  Recreating it here
384	                # would silently drop earlier revocation records.
385	                raise ValueError(f"revocation journal missing: {journal_path}")
386	            # Append-only: a single write in append mode only adds a record,
387	            # never rewriting history.
388	            with open(journal_path, "ab") as fh:
389	                fh.write(line)
390	                fh.flush()
391	                os.fsync(fh.fileno())
392	
393	            entry["revoked"].add(version)
394	            self._snapshot = snapshot
395	            self._manifest = disk_manifest
396	
397	    def is_revoked(self, key_id: str, version: int) -> bool:
398	        """Return whether ``version`` of ``key_id`` has been revoked."""
399	        _check_key_id(key_id)
400	        _check_version(version)
401	        entry = self._snapshot.get(key_id)
402	        if entry is None:
403	            raise KeyError(key_id)
404	        if version not in entry["versions"]:
405	            raise KeyError(f"{key_id!r} version {version!r}")
406	        return version in entry["revoked"]
407	
408	    def revoked_versions(self, key_id: str) -> list[int]:
409	        """Return the revoked versions of ``key_id``, ascending.
410	
411	        A key that has never been revoked — including an unknown key —
412	        yields an empty list.
413	        """
414	        _check_key_id(key_id)
415	        entry = self._snapshot.get(key_id)
416	        if entry is None:
417	            return []
418	        return sorted(entry["revoked"])

420	    def reload(self) -> None:
421	        """Re-read and validate the whole keyring, then swap the snapshot.
422	
423	        Never writes to disk.  The whole read-and-validate pass happens
424	        under both locks so it cannot interleave with a seal, revoke or
425	        repoint — in this process or any other: the reload reads either the
426	        complete old records or the complete newly persisted ones, and
427	        swapping in a snapshot read before a concurrent seal completed would
428	        resurrect an old snapshot and could later reuse its version numbers.
429	        On any validation failure the current in-memory snapshot is kept
430	        untouched.
431	        """
432	        with self._locked():
433	            snapshot, manifest = self._load_validated()
434	            self._snapshot = snapshot
435	            self._manifest = manifest
436	
437	    def manifest(self) -> dict:
438	        """Return a deep copy of the persisted manifest."""
439	        return copy.deepcopy(self._manifest)

445	    @contextlib.contextmanager
446	    def _file_lock(self):
447	        """Exclusive, blocking inter-process lock scoped to the vault dir.
448	
449	        The caller holds ``self._lock``; the lock file handle is opened
450	        lazily here so a vault that was released with :meth:`close` reopens
451	        ``vault.lock`` on demand and reacquires the very same lock.  A
452	        caller that cannot take the lock waits until it can; the lock is
453	        held for the whole disk operation and released only once the record
454	        is fully done.  Uses ``fcntl.flock`` where available and falls back
455	        to ``msvcrt.locking`` on Windows — standard library only, no
456	        network coordination.
457	        """
458	        fh = self._ensure_lock_file()
459	        if fcntl is not None:
460	            fcntl.flock(fh.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
461	            try:
462	                yield
463	            finally:
464	                fcntl.flock(fh.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)
465	        else:
466	            import msvcrt
467	
468	            fh.seek(0)
469	            while True:
470	                try:
471	                    msvcrt.locking(fh.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_LOCK, 1)
472	                    break
473	                except OSError:  # timed out waiting; keep waiting
474	                    time.sleep(0.05)
475	            try:
476	                yield
477	            finally:
478	                fh.seek(0)
479	                msvcrt.locking(fh.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_UNLCK, 1)
480	
481	    def _ensure_lock_file(self):
482	        """Open ``vault.lock`` if needed and return its handle.
483	
484	        Guarded by ``self._lock``.  After :meth:`close` the handle is
485	        reopened on the next operation; opening never writes vault data.
486	        """
487	        if self._lock_fh is None:
488	            self._lock_fh = open(self._root / LOCK_NAME, "a+b")
489	        return self._lock_fh
490	
491	    def _release_lock_file(self) -> None:
492	        """Close the lock file handle if one is open (no-op otherwise)."""
493	        fh = self._lock_fh
494	        if fh is not None:
495	            self._lock_fh = None
496	            fh.close()
497	
498	    @contextlib.contextmanager
499	    def _locked(self):
500	        """Hold the in-process lock and the inter-process file lock.
501	
502	        The threading lock is always taken first, so lock ordering is
503	        consistent and deadlock-free.
504	        """
505	        with self._lock:
506	            with self._file_lock():
507	                yield

509	    def _seal_record(
510	        self, key_id: str, material: bytes, derivation: dict | None
511	    ) -> int:
512	        """Append one version: shared body of ``seal`` and ``derive_seal``.
513	
514	        ``derivation`` is ``None`` for directly supplied material, otherwise
515	        ``{"salt": bytes, "iterations": int, "length": int}``.  All entry
516	        validation has already happened and, for derived material, the
517	        passphrase-derived bytes are all that ever reaches disk.
518	        """
519	        with self._locked():
520	            # Re-read and validate the persisted keyring under the
521	            # inter-process lock: another process may have sealed since
522	            # this handle last looked, and the next version number must be
523	            # allocated from the latest state on disk so concurrent seals
524	            # never duplicate or skip a version and never overwrite
525	            # historical material.
526	            snapshot, disk_manifest = self._load_validated()
527	            new_manifest = copy.deepcopy(disk_manifest)
528	            entry = new_manifest["keys"].setdefault(
529	                key_id, {"active": 0, "versions": []}
530	            )
531	            records = entry["versions"]
532	            new_version = records[-1]["version"] + 1 if records else 1
533	
534	            rel_file = (
535	                f"{MATERIALS_DIR}/{_encode_key_id(key_id)}/{new_version}.bin"
536	            )
537	            digest = hashlib.sha256(material).hexdigest()
538	
539	            record = {"version": new_version, "sha256": digest, "file": rel_file}
540	            if derivation is not None:
541	                # Base64 keeps the salt as JSON text; parameters travel with
542	                # this one version and are read back for verification.
543	                record["derivation"] = {
544	                    "salt": base64.b64encode(derivation["salt"]).decode("ascii"),
545	                    "iterations": derivation["iterations"],
546	                    "length": derivation["length"],
547	                }
548	
549	            # Write the material first, then flip the manifest.  The manifest
550	            # is the source of truth and is replaced atomically, so a crash
551	            # in between can never expose a half-recorded version; if the
552	            # manifest write itself fails, remove the material just written
553	            # so a failed seal leaves no orphan behind.
554	            material_path = self._root / rel_file
555	            material_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
556	            _atomic_write(material_path, material)
557	
558	            try:
559	                records.append(record)
560	                entry["active"] = new_version
561	                _atomic_write(self._root / MANIFEST_NAME, _dump_manifest(new_manifest))
562	            except BaseException:
563	                # ``new_manifest`` is a private deep copy and is simply
564	                # discarded; only the material written above needs cleanup.
565	                try:
566	                    material_path.unlink()
567	                except OSError:
568	                    pass
569	                raise
570	
571	            # ``snapshot`` was just built by ``_load_validated`` and is not
572	            # shared yet, so it can be extended in place before publishing.
573	            slot = snapshot.setdefault(
574	                key_id, {
575	                    "active": 0,
576	                    "versions": {},
577	                    "revoked": set(),
578	                    "derivations": {},
579	                }
580	            )
581	            slot["versions"][new_version] = material
582	            if derivation is not None:
583	                slot["derivations"][new_version] = dict(derivation)
584	            slot["active"] = new_version
585	            self._snapshot = snapshot
586	            self._manifest = new_manifest
587	            return new_version
588	
589	    def _is_fresh_dir(self) -> bool:
590	        for child in self._root.iterdir():
591	            if child.name == LOCK_NAME:
592	                # The lock file is a mutual-exclusion device, not vault
593	                # content; it says nothing about freshness.
594	                continue
595	            if (
596	                child.name == MATERIALS_DIR
597	                and child.is_dir()
598	                and not any(child.iterdir())
599	            ):
600	                continue
601	            return False
602	        return True

604	    def _load_validated(self) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
605	        """Read and validate the whole keyring from disk.
606	
607	        Returns ``(snapshot, manifest)``.  The snapshot carries each key's
608	        materials plus its revoked-version set and the active version
609	        implied by the append-only journals.  Raises ``ValueError`` if the
610	        manifest or either journal is corrupt or malformed, a stored
611	        material is missing or mismatches its record, the revocation
612	        journal revokes an unknown/duplicate version, or the activation
613	        journal repoints an unknown key or nonexistent version.
614	        """
615	        manifest_path = self._root / MANIFEST_NAME
616	        try:
617	            raw = manifest_path.read_bytes()
618	        except FileNotFoundError as exc:
619	            raise ValueError(f"manifest missing: {manifest_path}") from exc
620	        except OSError as exc:
621	            raise ValueError(f"manifest unreadable: {exc}") from exc
622	
623	        try:
624	            manifest = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
625	        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
626	            raise ValueError(f"manifest corrupt: {exc}") from exc
627	
628	        if not isinstance(manifest, dict):
629	            raise ValueError("manifest format invalid: not a JSON object")
630	        if manifest.get("format") != FORMAT_VERSION:
631	            raise ValueError("manifest format invalid: unsupported format")
632	        keys = manifest.get("keys")
633	        if not isinstance(keys, dict):
634	            raise ValueError("manifest format invalid: 'keys' must be an object")
635	
636	        root_resolved = self._root.resolve()
637	        snapshot: dict[str, dict] = {}
638	        for key_id, entry in keys.items():
639	            if not isinstance(key_id, str) or not isinstance(entry, dict):
640	                raise ValueError("manifest format invalid: bad key entry")
641	            records = entry.get("versions")
642	            active = entry.get("active")
643	            if not isinstance(records, list) or not records:
644	                raise ValueError(
645	                    f"manifest format invalid: key {key_id!r} has no versions"
646	                )
647	            if type(active) is not int:
648	                raise ValueError(
649	                    f"manifest format invalid: key {key_id!r} has bad active"
650	                )
651	
652	            versions: dict[int, bytes] = {}
653	            derivations: dict[int, dict] = {}
654	            previous = 0
655	            for record in records:
656	                if not isinstance(record, dict):
657	                    raise ValueError(
658	                        f"manifest format invalid: key {key_id!r} bad record"
659	                    )
660	                version = record.get("version")
661	                digest = record.get("sha256")
662	                rel_file = record.get("file")
663	                if type(version) is not int or version <= previous:
664	                    raise ValueError(
665	                        f"manifest format invalid: key {key_id!r} versions "
666	                        "must be strictly increasing"
667	                    )
668	                previous = version
669	                if (
670	                    not isinstance(digest, str)
671	                    or len(digest) != 64
672	                    or any(c not in "0123456789abcdef" for c in digest)
673	                ):
674	                    raise ValueError(
675	                        f"manifest format invalid: key {key_id!r} version "
676	                        f"{version} has bad sha256"
677	                    )
678	                if not isinstance(rel_file, str):
679	                    raise ValueError(
680	                        f"manifest format invalid: key {key_id!r} version "
681	                        f"{version} has bad file"
682	                    )
683	                resolved = (self._root / rel_file).resolve()
684	                if not resolved.is_relative_to(root_resolved):
685	                    raise ValueError(
686	                        f"manifest format invalid: key {key_id!r} version "
687	                        f"{version} file escapes the vault"
688	                    )
689	                try:
690	                    material = resolved.read_bytes()
691	                except OSError as exc:
692	                    raise ValueError(
693	                        f"material missing for key {key_id!r} version {version}"
694	                    ) from exc
695	                if hashlib.sha256(material).hexdigest() != digest:
696	                    raise ValueError(
697	                        f"material mismatch for key {key_id!r} version {version}"
698	                    )
699	
700	                parameters = record.get("derivation")
701	                if parameters is not None:
702	                    salt, iterations, length = self._validate_derivation_record(
703	                        key_id, version, parameters
704	                    )
705	                    # The passphrase never touches disk, so reload cannot
706	                    # re-run PBKDF2 against it.  It can still prove the
707	                    # record is self-consistent: the declared derived length
708	                    # must equal the number of bytes actually stored, and
709	                    # the material itself is already checked byte-for-byte
710	                    # against its sha256 above.  Callers confirm
711	                    # reproducibility by re-deriving with their passphrase.
712	                    if length != len(material):
713	                        raise ValueError(
714	                            f"derivation length mismatch for key {key_id!r} "
715	                            f"version {version}"
716	                        )
717	                    derivations[version] = {
718	                        "salt": salt,
719	                        "iterations": iterations,
720	                        "length": length,
721	                    }
722	                versions[version] = material
723	
724	            if active != previous:
725	                raise ValueError(
726	                    f"manifest format invalid: key {key_id!r} active version "
727	                    "does not match the latest sealed version"
728	                )
729	            snapshot[key_id] = {
730	                "active": active,
731	                "versions": versions,
732	                "revoked": set(),
733	                "derivations": derivations,
734	            }
735	
736	        self._load_revocations(snapshot)
737	        self._load_activations(snapshot)
738	        return snapshot, manifest

740	    @staticmethod
741	    def _validate_derivation_record(
742	        key_id: str, version: int, parameters: object
743	    ) -> tuple[bytes, int, int]:
744	        """Validate a persisted ``derivation`` object.
745	
746	        Returns ``(salt, iterations, length)``.  Raises ``ValueError`` for a
747	        missing/empty/undecodable salt or any non-integer or non-positive
748	        parameter — reload rejects records hand-edited out of band.
749	        """
750	        label = f"key {key_id!r} version {version}"
751	        if not isinstance(parameters, dict):
752	            raise ValueError(
753	                f"manifest format invalid: {label} has bad derivation"
754	            )
755	        salt_text = parameters.get("salt")
756	        iterations = parameters.get("iterations")
757	        length = parameters.get("length")
758	        if not isinstance(salt_text, str) or salt_text == "":
759	            raise ValueError(
760	                f"manifest format invalid: {label} derivation salt missing"
